doc: Eight columns by four latitudes (21, 0, -21, 60 degrees; Hadley 30: the deck window is 1 at +-21 and 0 at the equator and at 60) taking every branch of the rest scaling. Columns as (closed, open, street, continentality, deck strength): rest = open + street = 0 (the guard rest > 1e-9 is false: scale 1), 5e-10 (under the guard: scale 1, nothing divided), 2e-9 (over it, 1 - closed over rest is huge and min(1, .) gives 1), a large rest 0.45 that the deck leaves little room for (partial scale 0.56 on the deck rows, min(1, 1.11) = 1 off the decks), closed = 1 with rest 0 (guard), closed = 1 with rest 0.5 (scale exactly 0: 1 - closed = 0), a half-land texel with rest 0.75 (scale 0.24 on the decks), and a full land texel (continentality 1: closed 0.9 becomes 0, then the deck fills it to 1 on the deck rows: scale 0). Out-of-contract sums (closed + rest > 1) are used on purpose where needed. Float32 outputs; the numerics include the float32 rounding of 1 - closed (spelled out under Arguments below). The guard threshold itself (1e-9) and the inner floor are pinned only between 5e-10 and 2e-9 here: the decades between 1e-9 and 1e-3 are surface_regime_weights.tiny_rest. Arguments: the weights (w_closed, w_open, w_street = the dict entries closed, open, street), continentality and deck_strength (the two SurfaceTerms fields the function reads; the others are not read) and lat_rows (the latitude of each row in rad, broadcast over the columns as generate() does); hadley_deg is in params. Outputs closed, open, street (float32). Dtype chain to reproduce: sea = 1 - continentality and closed = w_closed sea are float32; deck = deck_window(x) deck_strength is float64 (x from the float64 latitudes); in closed + (1 - closed) deck the factor (1 - closed) is rounded to float32 BEFORE it meets the float64 deck, so closed (float64 from there on) can land a few 1e-8 above 1 and the scale (1 - closed) / rest then comes out slightly NEGATIVE (down to about -2.3e-8 on the open and street shares); the source does not clamp it and the stored outputs keep it. A float64 end-to-end port, or one that clamps the scale at 0, differs from this by at most that much (2.3e-8 on the stored cases), inside the tolerance: the negative shares are an artifact of that float32 rounding, not a contract. Measured: promoting the float32 inputs to float64 changes the output by at most 1.5e-8; one-ulp nudges of every float input and parameter change it by at most 1.2e-7 (worst of 6 random trials); the tolerance is 19x the larger of the two spreads.
